channel.title: Japan AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Japan's political, economic and security developments

item.title: 11-year-old esports prodigy Yuki Kurihara claims gold at Asian Games
item.description: He is the youngest athlete in Japan's Asian Games history.

item.title: Junglia theme park in Okinawa logs ¥17 billion loss in first year
item.description: The ¥70 billion park opened last July to high expectations that it would help extend tourist stays and boost the local economy.

item.title: Japan’s finance chief says Takaichi isn’t ‘reflationist’
item.description: The finance minister also reiterated her readiness to again support the yen and played down jitters over the recent gains in bond yields.

item.title: Japan’s bond ‘falling knife’ stalls repatriation rush
item.description: Major investors remain reluctant to commit heavily to domestic bonds while yields are still climbing and few clues about how much rates must rise.

item.title: Yen rises as Japanese officials say weak currency is problem
item.description: The currency strengthened as much as 1.2%, the most since Sept. 7, to ¥156.94 per dollar on Friday, outperforming all of its Group-of-10 peers.

item.title: When tourists do the ‘Nagoya skip,’ do they know what they’re skipping?
item.description: Despite historical, cultural and culinary draws, only 10% of overseas visitors set foot in Aichi and Gifu prefectures.

item.title: Japanese skateboarders grab gold at Asian Games
item.description: In swimming, Kodai Nishiono won the gold medal in the men's 200-meter backstroke.

item.title: Storm menaces Japan after highest cyclone tally since 1966
item.description: Tropical Storm Surigae is currently 791 kilometers south-southeast of Okinawa, packing top sustained winds of 74 kilometers per hour.

item.title: Japan regulator is boosting scrutiny of AI data center financing
item.description: The move comes as major financial institutions increase their exposure to the rapidly expanding sector.

item.title: Japan to expand disaster preparedness with new national agency
item.description: The National Disaster Management Agency will be launched on Nov. 2 and serve as the government's command center for disaster preparedness.

item.title: Japan growth minister says economy has exited reflationary phase
item.description: Minoru Kiuchi's comments follow renewed weakness in the yen and further gains in government bond yields this week.

item.title: Say where? Japanese towns use self-deprecating humor for tourism boost
item.description: Some municipalities are flipping their low name recognition into opportunities for self-promotion.

item.title: Swiss franc, Japanese yen Rise as DeepSeek News Boosts Safe Havens
item.description: The Yen and Swiss Franc were stronger against the dollar as investors sought safe havens after Chinese start-up DeepSeek’s new AI model hit U.S. tech stocks.
